final_message:
I fixed two bugs in `wrap` in `src/wrap.py`. I haven't run it or any tests.

1. **Off-by-one on width:** the check was `> width - 1`, so lines wrapped one character early and never reached the full `width`. It is now `> width`.
2. **Empty first line:** a first word longer than `width` pushed an empty string onto `lines`. The wrap check now only fires when the current line isn't empty, so that word goes on its own line.

Words longer than `width` stay unbroken. I assumed that behavior is wanted. If you want them split across lines, tell me.
